videos.caption: Listen to the pain in his voice. The endless suffering of Palestinians in Gaza. ENOUGH IS ENOUGH! Thousands of tents broke overnight, and this young boy in Zaytoun neighborhood is one of them. The Sameer Project is getting hundreds of calls and messages asking for support, and we don’t have the funds to do it! The military occupation closed the Egyptian borders a few days ago, and there are no tents or tarps coming in. War profiteers supported by the military occupation are hoarding tents and tarps, and hiking the prices making it impossible for anyone to afford them. Our choices are to feel hopeless and angry, or mobilize and help as much as we can. The Sameer Project chooses the latter but we NEED your urgent help. Donate urgently to the General Fund and share the crisis in Gaza with everyone you know.

🚨 ADI KARNI: “I’M AN IDF SOLDIER, ASK ME ANYTHING!” — PRO-PALESTINIAN STUDENTS CONFRONT HIM AT CALIFORNIA UNIVERSITY 🇵🇸 Israeli social media creator Adi Karni arrived at California State University, Long Beach (CSULB), on November 16, wearing an Israeli flag and holding a sign inviting students to ask him anything about the IDF. But his appearance outside the university library quickly attracted a large crowd of students who opposed his presence on campus. Students surrounded the area, chanting “FREE, FREE PALESTINE!” and demanding that he leave. Campus police eventually intervened and escorted Karni away from the confrontation. The incident comes amid continuing student protests across American universities over Israel’s military operations in Gaza and the role of individuals associated with the Israeli military in public campus events. Karni later claimed that protesters threw rocks at him, although this allegation has not been independently verified in the reporting available. The confrontation has reignited discussions about freedom of expression, campus protests and the ongoing debate surrounding Palestine. 🇵🇸 STUDENTS MADE THEIR POSITION CLEAR. 🌍 Follow @echoofgeopolitics for daily global news and perspectives.
